questions.q: What does RFM stand for in this project's segmentation?
options: Recency, Frequency, Monetary
Region, Frequency, Margin
Recency, Filter, Metric
Ranking, Frequency, Model
questions.explain: RFM segments customers by Recency (how recently they ordered), Frequency (how often), and Monetary value (how much they spent).

questions.q: Why does the lesson specify that Recency, Frequency, and Monetary should be built as FIXED LOD expressions?
options: Because each metric needs to be computed at the customer level, independent of whatever other dimensions are on a given view
Because FIXED LOD expressions are always faster than any other calculation type
Because Tableau requires all customer-level metrics to use FIXED
Because table calculations cannot reference the Customer Name field
questions.explain: A FIXED LOD expression locks the calculation to a specified level of detail (here, per customer) regardless of what else is in the view, which is exactly what per-customer Recency, Frequency, and Monetary values require.

questions.q: What should the segmentation calculated field produce, according to the rubric?
options: Business-readable segment names like "Champions" or "At Risk," never generic labels like "Segment 1"
A single numeric score with no labels at all
The customer's raw Sales total, unchanged
A random assignment of customers to segments
questions.explain: The rubric explicitly calls for business-readable segment names, not generic numbered labels, so the dashboard reads clearly to a non-technical viewer.

questions.q: What should the scatter plot in this project encode, at minimum?
options: Two RFM metrics on the axes, segment as color, and the third RFM metric as size — one dot per customer
Only a single RFM metric, repeated on both axes
Product categories instead of customers
Order dates only, with no other encoding
questions.explain: The lesson requires at least three dimensions of information encoded in the scatter plot (two axes, color, size) so it communicates real segmentation structure, not just a single measure.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend manually verifying the RFM calculated fields against two or three individual customers before trusting the segmentation built on top of them?
options: Because a FIXED LOD expression with the wrong dimension will silently produce wrong values, and every downstream segment inherits that error
Because Tableau does not allow LOD expressions to be tested
Because manual verification is required before any calculated field can be saved
Because customer-level data is always unreliable
questions.explain: Getting the FIXED dimension wrong in an LOD expression produces incorrect per-customer values without any visible error — spot-checking against known customers catches that before it propagates into the segmentation logic.
